transcript.assistant: Yes, you did — a Saturday evening in June, about three months back. You'd gone to a drop-in wheel-throwing class on your own that afternoon, the first time you'd touched clay since school, and your bowl collapsed twice before Ines, the teacher, who had clay right up to her elbows, came over and had you make a very small cup instead. The cup leaned to one side, you said, like it was listening to something, and you'd picked a seafoam glaze for it, with firing the following week. Your forearms were already aching, and you said you hadn't felt that pleased with yourself in months.
transcript.user: Didn't I tell you once about a time I had a go at pottery myself? How did that go? I can barely remember it now.
